subject: [PATCH v3 1/3] mm/swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator

2026-08-25.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator. The previous behavior added the folio to the LRU immediately, but this change defers the insertion until the caller is ready to act on the folio. This is necessary for two upcoming patches: one that moves refault evaluation out of the swap cache allocation and another that implements zswap writeback dropbehind. The functional changes are minimal, as each caller will add the folio to the LRU after allocation.

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Usama Arif pointed out that the patch description should follow kernel conventions by avoiding references to future patches and their potential landing locations.

reviews.raw_body:
I think the kernel convention is to not say "next patch" and "upcoming.."

Especially as this patch is in 2 series, so you don't know where it will land.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not address a potential issue where __swap_cache_alloc_folio() is called from multiple places, and some of these callers may not be prepared to handle the folio being added to the LRU immediately.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti expressed uncertainty about handling a shared patch, but agreed to drop references as suggested by Usama Arif.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the patch moves the LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator, but did not provide any specific feedback or concerns.

2026-08-26.patch_summary: This patch moves the LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator, allowing callers to act on the allocated folio before it becomes visible to reclaim. This change is necessary because some users need to set flags or perform other actions on the folio before it's added to the LRU. The patch updates the swap_cache_alloc_folio function to return a private allocation and defers the LRU insertion to the callers, which can then add the folio to the LRU as needed.
